summary: Set up nginx on node1 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 using a self-signed certificate managed by an automated renewal pipeline (renew-cert.sh + cert-renew.service/timer). The timer checks cert expiry daily (openssl x509 -checkend against a 15-day window on 30-day certs) and, when a cert is due, atomically regenerates key/cert and does `systemctl reload nginx` for zero-downtime pickup. Verified the full pipeline live: installed a near-expiry test cert, fired the same service unit the timer invokes, and confirmed nginx renewed the cert and reloaded while 80 concurrent HTTPS polls all returned 200 with no failures, and the live TLS handshake immediately served the new certificate. Also configured firewalld (8443/tcp) and SELinux (http_port_t) for the port, and enabled nginx + cert-renew.timer to start on boot. Completed the mandatory node1 restart: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy service/cert state, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified nginx, the renewal timer, firewall/SELinux config, and the HTTPS endpoint (serving the same renewed cert) all recovered post-restart.
actions_performed: Installed nginx and policycoreutils-python-utils on node1
Added SELinux http_port_t label and firewalld permanent rule for tcp/8443
Created /usr/local/sbin/renew-cert.sh implementing checkend-based renewal with atomic cert/key swap and nginx reload
Created and enabled cert-renew.service (oneshot) and cert-renew.timer (daily, OnBootSec=2min, Persistent=true)
Issued the initial self-signed cert (CN=node1, SAN=IP/DNS) and deployed nginx vhost /etc/nginx/conf.d/https-8443.conf listening ssl on 8443
Enabled and started nginx and cert-renew.timer
Simulated a near-expiry cert and fired cert-renew.service (the same unit the timer invokes) while continuously polling HTTPS to prove zero-downtime renewal and reload
Verified live TLS handshake serves the newly renewed certificate

Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline, executed systemctl reboot on node1, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified nginx/timer/firewall/SELinux/HTTPS/cert state post-restart

evidence.requirement: HTTPS served on port 8443 with a valid certificate
evidence.summary: nginx configured with ssl vhost on 8443, cert issued, firewalld/SELinux opened, curl to https://$NODE_IP:8443 returns http_code=200

evidence.requirement: Certificate renewed automatically before expiry via a timer mechanism
evidence.summary: cert-renew.service/timer created and enabled; live test with a near-expiry cert shows the service (same one the timer fires) detects the expiry window via openssl checkend and renews the cert (new serial 477746D9... with notAfter Oct 29 2026)

evidence.requirement: Service picks up new certificate while continuing to answer requests (no downtime)
evidence.summary: 80 continuous HTTPS polls spanning the renewal all returned 200 with zero failures; nginx reload log confirms 'nginx reloaded'; live TLS handshake immediately serves the new cert serial matching the on-disk cert
Captured boot_id f54d7366-..., nginx active, cert-renew.timer active, HTTPS 200, cert serial/expiry recorded

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged before disconnect, node unreachable mid-reboot, then reachable again with new boot_id 5de60926-... (uptime since 07:45:27) proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services, data, and config
evidence.summary: nginx and cert-renew.timer both active post-restart, timer correctly scheduled, HTTPS still returns 200 serving the same persisted renewed certificate, firewalld port and SELinux port label persisted, live TLS handshake cert matches on-disk cert
